content.topic: Percutaneous edge-to-edge mitral valve repair for secondary mitral regurgitation (SMR)
content.summary: Two randomized trials (MITRA-FR and COAPT) compared percutaneous edge-to-edge mitral valve repair + optimal medical therapy (OMT) versus OMT alone in symptomatic patients with secondary MR. MITRA-FR did not show benefit on all-cause mortality or HF hospitalization, while COAPT showed a significant reduction in HF hospitalization and a secondary reduction in mortality. Differences in patient selection, severity of SMR, LV dilatation and other procedural/echocardiographic factors likely explain divergent results. Percutaneous edge-to-edge repair may be considered in carefully selected symptomatic patients despite OMT, with specific anatomical and echocardiographic inclusion criteria (based on COAPT) and in selected patients with advanced HF where other options such as transplant or LVAD should also be considered.

trials.name: MITRA-FR
trials.finding: Failed to show benefit from percutaneous edge-to-edge mitral valve repair on all-cause mortality or HF hospitalization at 12 months (primary endpoint) and at 24 months.
trials.notes: Effective regurgitant orifice area (EROA) inclusion around ≥20 mm^2 (as stated in text). Differences in patient selection and severity of SMR cited as possible reasons for neutral result.

trials.name: COAPT
trials.finding: Showed significant reduction in HF hospitalization at 24 months (primary endpoint) and a reduction in mortality as a secondary endpoint.
trials.notes: EROA inclusion around ≥30 mm^2 (as stated). COAPT inclusion criteria referenced (see selection_criteria).

MITRA-FR.outcome_summary: No benefit on all-cause mortality or HF hospitalization at 12 and 24 months.

COAPT.outcome_summary: Significant reduction in HF hospitalization at 24 months and reduction in mortality (secondary endpoint).
COAPT.reported_effects: Hazard ratios and confidence intervals are cited in the text for hospitalization and mortality (e.g., HR ~0.53 for hospitalization; HR ~0.62 for mortality) although exact formatting was partially garbled in the source image.

selection_criteria_for_consideration.symptom_status: Patients who remain symptomatic (NYHA class II–IV) despite OMT
selection_criteria_for_consideration.SMR_severity: Moderate-to-severe or severe secondary mitral regurgitation (EROA thresholds referenced; COAPT used EROA ≥30 mm^2)
selection_criteria_for_consideration.left_ventricular_function_and_dimensions: COAPT-like criteria (example in text: LVEF ~20–50%, LV end-systolic diameter <70 mm)
selection_criteria_for_consideration.hemodynamics_and_right_heart: Systolic pulmonary pressure <70 mmHg, absence of moderate or severe RV dysfunction
selection_criteria_for_consideration.other: Favourable anatomical conditions and fulfillment of COAPT inclusion criteria; absence of severe tricuspid regurgitation and haemodynamic instability

clinical_recommendations: Consider percutaneous edge-to-edge mitral valve repair for outcome improvement only in carefully selected patients who remain symptomatic despite OMT and who meet anatomical and echocardiographic criteria similar to those used in COAPT.

In patients with advanced HF and severe SMR who remain symptomatic despite OMT, consider percutaneous repair to improve symptoms; also evaluate candidacy for cardiac transplantation or LVAD where appropriate.

other_percutaneous_options.notes: Available for SMR treatment; shorter learning curve and lesser technical requirements. A sham-controlled randomized trial reported reduction in mitral regurgitant volume with reverse LV and LA remodeling at 12 months.
Emerging possible alternative option; randomized trials are still lacking.

content.evidence_limitations_and_interpretation: Differences in patient selection, concomitant therapies, echocardiographic assessment, procedural issues and severity of SMR in relation to LV dilatation may explain divergent results between trials. Randomized data for some emerging transcatheter solutions remain limited.
